transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Severus! My crystallized pineapple is ruined — that jar was a gift from the Minister himself! And you've used my personal cauldron without asking! I have the Potions Guild inspection in two hours and the storeroom looks like a hippogriff went through it. You promised to keep it tidy!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The crystallized pineapple? Slughorn, it's summer, the jar was unsealed, and the heat has taken its toll. As for your cauldron, I had urgent business that could not wait, and it was the only one available. This disarray is not entirely my doing; someone else has been in here.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Unsealed? Severus, that jar was a special preservative charm! It doesn't simply "unseal" itself. And even if it *had*, a competent guardian of this storeroom – which *you* were meant to be – would have noticed and re-sealed it, or at least moved it to a cooler spot! This isn't just any old pineapple, it was a gesture of… well, never mind.

And "urgent business"? What urgent business requires *my* personally charmed, temperature-regulated cauldron, when there are perfectly adequate lesser cauldrons all over the place? "Only one available"? Don't be absurd, you know perfectly well where the spares are kept!

And now you blame "someone else"? Who, pray tell, has been rummaging through *my* private storeroom? And why weren't *you* here to stop them? This *is* your doing, Severus, or your utter failure to prevent it! The Potions Guild inspectors will be here any moment, and I simply cannot present this… this *pigsty*! My reputation!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Inspection? You scheduled a Potions Guild inspection during the summer term when no classes are in session? How shortsighted of you, Slughorn. As for my "failure to prevent" it, you conveniently neglect to mention that we are sharing these quarters. My efforts to maintain order have been repeatedly undone by your... let's call it 'lax' approach to tidiness.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Shortsighted? Severus, the Guild *always* inspects during the summer to ensure year-round excellence and to catch us unawares! It's a test of preparedness, which *you* have clearly failed! I scheduled it because I expected a responsible assistant to *maintain* the storeroom, not turn it into a… a brewing disaster zone!

And don't you dare try to shift the blame onto my "lax approach"! My approach is to trust my colleagues to uphold standards! This isn't *my* mess, Severus! My "lax approach," as you so charmingly put it, involves *expecting* people to put things back where they belong, to *not* use my personal equipment without so much as a by-your-leave, and to *definitely* not allow rare, gifted consumables to spoil! Look at this! It's an utter disgrace! How am I to explain this to Augustus Rookwood, let alone the Guild Master?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Augustus Rookwood? The man whose fondness for飞天螞蟻酒 borders on the unhealthy? I'm sure he'll be quite forgiving of a few misplaced jars, especially considering the state of his own personal collection. As for the Guild Master, perhaps you should explain to him why a professor at Hogwarts, who should have better things to do, has taken it upon himself to rearrange the contents of a shared storeroom to better suit his whims.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Horace's face goes a shade of puce, his eyes bulging slightly.)

Rookwood's personal predilections are entirely beside the point, Severus! And how *dare* you imply that *I* am rearranging the storeroom for my "whims"! This is a professional space, maintained for the precise storage of rare ingredients and equipment! My "whims" are about *order* and *efficiency*, which clearly you neither understand nor value!

A professor at Hogwarts *should* have better things to do than clean up after his slovenly colleague, yes! That is precisely my point! My time should be spent preparing for the inspection, ensuring my lecture notes are pristine, perhaps even enjoying a quiet moment before the storm, not wading through a chaos of your making!

The Guild Master expects a certain standard, Severus! A standard that *I* have always upheld, and a standard that *you* are making it utterly impossible for me to present! This is an embarrassment! Look at that shelf! Is that a Flobberworm mucus vial next to the powdered moonstone? They'll think I've gone mad!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see no Flobberworm mucus here, Slughorn. It appears to be dragon scale. And as for your standards, you may rest assured that the inspectors will find the department in pristine condition, assuming you manage to present anything beyond your own emotional instability. Now, if you will allow me to finish what I came here to do, perhaps we can both benefit from the remaining time before the inspection.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Horace peers closer, fumbling for his spectacles, then snorts in irritation)

Dragon scale! Well, it's certainly not in its *designated* place, is it? And it certainly doesn't belong *there*! My standards, Severus, involve a meticulous, organised environment, not a guessing game of "what's this vaguely slimy substance today?"

"Emotional instability"? Is that what you call a legitimate and entirely justified outrage at finding one's storeroom in utter disarray, one's precious gifts ruined, and one's personal equipment used without so much as a thought for courtesy or respect, just two hours before a crucial inspection?! I call it *passion* for excellence!

And what, pray tell, is this urgent task you "came here to do" that takes precedence over tidying up the monumental mess you've either created or, worse, *allowed* to fester?! We both benefit, you say? The only benefit I can see is if you finally pull yourself together and help me salvage what little dignity I have left before Augustus Rookwood and his clipboard arrive! Move it, Severus! Now! We haven't got all day!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: If you wish to retain any dignity, Slughorn, I suggest you lower your voice and tone down your theatrics. The inspection is not for another hour and a half, and between the two of us, we can rectify this situation with relative ease, assuming we can avoid further... melodrama. As for my task, it is a matter of personal importance, but it can wait. Let us address the more immediate issue at hand.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Horace glares, his cheeks still flushed, but the mention of "melodrama" stings him slightly, making him bridle rather than escalate further. He takes a deep, wheezing breath, gesturing wildly around the room.)

Melodrama? Severus, this is a catastrophe! An absolute disaster! But… very well. An hour and a half, you say? It feels like minutes!

So, you admit it can be rectified with "relative ease"? So you *acknowledge* the mess then! Good. A start, at least. And your "personal importance" can wait? Oh, how magnanimous of you! As if *anything* could be more important than averting utter humiliation for the Head of House!

Right then. No more bickering. We haven't the time. You! Start with those shelves over there – the ones with the labelled jars, *correctly* labelled, mind you. Ensure they're all facing forward, clean, and in alphabetical order! And for Merlin's sake, put the volatile components on the bottom shelf, not eye-level! I don't need a minor explosion during an inspection! I'll tackle this ghastly pile of… of whatever this is… over here. And for goodness sake, try not to look like you're sucking on a lemon, Severus. We need to project an image of calm, professional competence, even if it's utterly fabricated!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Calm, professional competence is not a facade I need to fabricate, Slughorn. It is, however, a state you might benefit from achieving yourself. Nonetheless, as you have assigned the tasks, I shall proceed accordingly. The volatile components are well within reach of the average Potions student, but I see your point. I shall take care to ensure their proper placement. Now, if you would kindly refrain from hovering, I can make faster progress.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Horace bristles slightly at the barb but forces himself to take another deep, slightly shaky breath. He watches Severus for a moment, then sighs, running a hand over his thinning hair.)

Yes, yes, well... just see that it gets done, Severus. Quickly. And *properly*. "Well within reach," you say? The Guild has very specific guidelines for hazardous materials, you know! Safety first! Always!

(He moves to his own assigned pile, bending over with a grunt. He picks up a stray vial, peering at its contents with a grimace.)

I'm not "hovering," Severus, I'm... supervising. And ensuring *my* side of the room is tackled with the appropriate urgency! Now, where on earth did this come from? It's clearly a student's attempt at a hair-thickening potion, judging by the rather suspicious clump of what appears to be... rather coarse animal fur. Disgusting. The nerve! You'd think they'd have enough respect not to leave their experimental failures in a *professional* storeroom! This is why we can't have nice things, Severus. This is precisely why!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(Severus, who has been methodically sorting and arranging the contents of the shelves, does not look up from his task. He speaks in a tone that suggests he's neither surprised nor particularly perturbed by Horace's latest discovery.)

It is fortunate, then, that we have the means to dispose of such... "experiments" efficiently. The bin is in the corner, next to the fume hood. I trust you are familiar with its location, given that you seem to have an intimate knowledge of the detritus it often contains. If you would cease your diatribe and remove the... clump of interest, we can both resume our respective tasks with greater alacrity. The hour is indeed late, and there is much to be done.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Horace splutters slightly, momentarily speechless at Severus's calm cheek. He clutches the offending vial as if it might explode.)

My "intimate knowledge of the detritus"? Severus! Are you implying I'm responsible for *student* detritus? I simply *noticed* it! It was practically screaming for attention, quite unlike some of the other, more… *subtle* messes I've found around here!

(He marches over to the bin, dropping the vial in with a clink and a rather dramatic sigh of disgust, then wipes his hands on a pristine handkerchief he pulls from his pocket.)

Right. Very well. No more diatribes. Just… action. Pure, unadulterated action. I'm just trying to ensure everything is perfect, Severus! Absolutely perfect! My reputation, you see. It precedes me. And I'd rather it didn't precede me as the Keeper of the Pigsty. Just… get on with it. And remember, alphabetical! A-L on the top two shelves, M-Z on the bottom two. It's not rocket science, it's basic organisation!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am well aware of your need for order, Slughorn. Your meticulousness is... a point of pride for you. However, if you wish to be of any assistance, perhaps you could focus your efforts on the area around the cauldron you so fervently defend. The charred remains of what I assume was once a batch of crystallized lemon drops have a rather unpleasant aroma. Given the time constraints, I would suggest we prioritize the most visible areas. The inspectors will not be examining the undersides of the shelves, after all.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Horace's eyes dart to his personal cauldron, then to the floor around it. A faint blush creeps up his neck.)

The… the crystallized lemon drops? Oh, that! A minor, ah, mishap from an *earlier* experiment. Entirely unrelated to… well, never mind. It was merely a test of a new rapid-crystallisation charm, you understand. Highly innovative work, Severus! The aroma… yes, it is rather potent, isn't it? A testament to the charm's *efficacy*, if not its immediate palatability!

(He clears his throat, ignoring the implied criticism.)

You're quite right, of course. Prioritise the visible. Excellent suggestion. See, we *can* work together when we put our minds to it! Right. The cauldron. Yes. I'll get to it immediately. A quick Scourgify and a few discreet Fresh Air Charms should do the trick. Just keep at those shelves, Severus. Remember, perfection is the goal! Utter, undeniable perfection!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Perfection, indeed. I trust your Fresh Air Charms will not inadvertently send the charred remains of your lemon experiment into a convenient gust of wind. In any case, if we are to achieve the standard of excellence you so clearly desire, I suggest we maintain our focus. Time is of the essence, and the inspectors will soon be upon us. If you would prefer not to discuss your experimental failures, I would be happy to simply ignore the distinctive scent that now lingers in the air.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Horace winces slightly at the continued jab, but his focus is already shifting to the scorched area around his cauldron. He waves his wand, muttered a quick cleaning charm, and a puff of grey ash vanishes.)

Severus, please! My Fresh Air Charms are of the highest calibre! There'll be no uncontrolled gusts, I assure you! And the lemon drop incident was hardly a *failure*, merely… an *unexpected outcome*! A learning experience, if you will!

(He fusses over the cauldron, polishing it with a vigorous motion, then casts a scent-neutralising charm with a slightly more flourish than necessary.)

Right. There! Much better. See? Efficiency! No need to ignore anything, Severus, when a simple charm can rectify such… such *minor* atmospheric anomalies. Now, back to it! Are those vials on the third shelf truly in alphabetical order? I see… is that Valerian next to… Venom? Hmm. A little too close for comfort, wouldn't you say? Especially with Augustus's particularly… *keen* sense of detail!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Valerian and Venom are, in fact, adjacent in the alphabet. Your concern, while appreciated, is unwarranted. However, if you feel the need to rearrange them for greater visual appeal, I will not object. I would, however, recommend against spending an inordinate amount of time on such a trivial matter. There are far more pressing issues at hand, such as the state of the cupboard where the essences are stored. It appears to have been ransacked by an enthusiastic Beater during魁地奇 season.
